title: Distributions of molecules in the circumnuclear disk and surrounding starburst ring in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 observed with ALMA
question: How are molecules distributed between the circumnuclear disk and the starburst ring of NGC 1068, and what does this say about AGN and starburst effects on molecular abundances?

what.value: Star formation rates of regions in the starburst ring

evidence.quote: we studied the relation of methanol intensity to the star-formation rate (cite: tsai2012) in those regions with relatively strong methanol emission

what.value: IRAM 30m 13CO flux (12.8 K km/s) and C18O/13CO ratio 0.28

evidence.loc: 3.4 Comparison of flux with single dish telescopes
evidence.quote: The corresponding value obtained with the 30m telescope is $\sim$12.8 K km s$^{-1}$ (cite: aladro2013)

recipe.method: Moment 0 maps from cubes using all pixel flux values

recipe.goal: Extract spectra at AGN and SW ring and fit lines
recipe.method: Spectra from cleaned images (beam-matched, PB-corrected) at the continuum peak and 13CO 3-2 peak; Gaussian fits

recipe.goal: Measure CND and total flux and ratio
recipe.method: Flux in 10'' circle (CND) and 55'' circle (total) centered on the continuum peak; ratio CND/Total used for classification

recipe.goal: Check flux recovery against single dishes
recipe.method: Convolve ALMA PB-corrected data to the 45m and 30m beams and compare K km/s

evidence.loc: 3.4 Comparison of flux with single dish telescopes
evidence.quote: Therefore, the recovered flux is about 92 %.
